Context/Background: Perianal fistulizing Crohn’s disease (CD) is a severe gastrointestinal disorder causing extensive mucosal damage with limited treatment options. Severe manifestations of the disease appear at higher rates in non-Europeans but the genetic and cellular mechanisms driving the disease phenotypes remain poorly understood. Herein, we tested whether pathologic determinants in the epithelial stem cell compartment could be detected at the transcript level in rectal organoids derived from a diverse patient population. Rectal organoid and mucosal cells from endoscopic biopsies of each patient having perianal fistulizing CD or no disease controls were prepared for and sequenced at the single cell level. After cell type annotations based on expressed marker genes, samples were analyzed by principal components, for differential transcript expression, cell type proportions, and pathway enrichment.
Prompt: Pathway analysis of transcriptional data from the organoids of different CD phenotypes was performed against the Reactome database.  CD phenotypes compared are: PIF (Perianal CD inflamed) vs PNI (Perianal CD non inflamed), PIF vs Control (non IBD), and PIN vs Control.  Please give a summary of the pathway enrichment results.  Focus on the comparisons involving the PIF (inflamed) group.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
The uploaded Table (41598_2024_75947_MOESM1_ESM-S1.csv) lists Reactome pathways significantly enriched among differentially expressed genes in rectal organoids from Perianal Fistulizing CD (PIF), Perianal non-inflamed CD (PNI), and non-IBD controls.  The table reports for each pathway: member genes, “GeneCount/direction” (signed count of DE genes), “Direction” (UP/DOWN in PIF), and the comparison (PIFvsPNI or PIFvsCtrl).  No sample sizes or p-values are shown; only gene counts and directionality are provided.

Keywords  
• Innate immunity  
• Lipid metabolism  
• Cell cycle  
• Stress response  
• Neutrophil degranulation  

Candidate Genes  
NFKB1, MAPK3, TRIB3, PSMA7  

Summary of PIF-related Comparisons  

PIF vs PNI  
• All 58 significant pathways are DOWN in PIF vs PNI.  
• Top suppressed pathways by |GeneCount|:  
  – Innate Immune System (114 genes DOWN)  
  – Metabolism of Lipids (96 genes DOWN)  
  – Infectious Disease (89 genes DOWN)  
  – Cell Cycle (79 genes DOWN)  
• Other repressed modules include Cellular Responses to Stimuli (77 DOWN), Cellular Stress (77 DOWN), Neutrophil Degranulation (74 DOWN), RTK Signaling (63 DOWN), Amino Acid Metabolism (44 DOWN), Rho GTPase Effectors (37 DOWN), Programmed Cell Death (35 DOWN), and Chemical Stress Response (33 DOWN).

PIF vs Control  
• All 54 significant pathways are also DOWN in PIF vs non-IBD controls.  
• Top suppressed pathways:  
  – Metabolism of Lipids (92 genes DOWN)  
  – Cellular Responses to Stimuli (74 DOWN)  
  – Cellular Responses to Stress (73 DOWN)  
  – Neutrophil Degranulation (64 DOWN)  

Interpretation  
Organoids derived from inflamed PIF patients show broad transcriptional downregulation of innate immunity, metabolic processes (especially lipid and amino acid metabolism), cell-cycle progression, neutrophil degranulation, and stress-response pathways compared both to non-inflamed CD (PNI) and non-IBD controls.  This concordant suppression suggests that epithelial stem cells in PIF may be depleted of proliferative and defense capacities, with impaired metabolic and stress-handling functions, potentially contributing to barrier dysfunction and fistula pathology.

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Validate key downregulated genes (e.g., NFKB1, MAPK3, TRIB3, PSMA7) by qPCR or protein assays in independent PIF organoids.  
2. Assess whether the suppressed innate-immune signature in PIF is recapitulated at the single-cell level in other epithelial subtypes.  
3. Test functional consequences of lipid metabolism downregulation (e.g., membrane integrity assays).  
4. Clarify whether cell-cycle pathway suppression reflects stem-cell quiescence or loss.
